text:
ana: Onboarding attempt for iris-7b-v2 (hf://models/team/iris-7b-v2) — staging mirror failed checksum on shard 00003. HF sha256 vs our S3 object's hash don't match. Anyone seen this pattern before?

raj: I saw something similar last month — usually presign/redirects or CF gzip getting in the way. Which job ran the ingest?

ana: it's the `onboard-weights` CI job triggered by the registry webhook. It used the registry presign flow with ttl=900. Manifest expected size 524,288,000; S3 reported 524,287,794. sha256(HF)="3a7f9...b1c2" vs sha256(S3)="3a7f9...c0d3" (diff near tail).

mike: Short, common causes: truncated download, transparent compression, or double-transfer corruption. Also saw tokenizers with null bos/eos that fail our validation if we run `validate-tokenizer` during onboard. Did the tokenizer.json have null tokens?

ana: Yup tokenizer.json has "bos_token": null, "eos_token": null. Our loader tolerates some shapes but the onboard linter bails.

tess: Quick note on presign: our registry sometimes returns a CloudFront URL for staging with redirects. If the client doesn't follow redirects or CF applies `Content-Encoding: gzip` for certain Accept-Encoding combinations we get size diffs. CI agent uses `curl --fail --silent` which doesn't always follow 307 with the same headers.

oliver: Can you paste the manifest header and the `aws s3api head-object` output for the object? Also what exact presign URL was used (redacted ok)?

ana: Pasting minimal bits: ```json
{
  "path": "s3://redwood-artifacts/staging/iris-7b-v2/pytorch_model-00003-of-00012.bin",
  "size": 524288000,
  "sha256": "3a7f9...b1c2",
  "origin": "hf",
  "origin_url": "https://huggingface.co/team/iris-7b-v2/resolve/main/pytorch_model-00003-of-00012.bin"
}```
Head-object: ```bash
$ aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-artifacts --key staging/iris-7b-v2/pytorch_model-00003-of-00012.bin
{
  "ContentLength": 524287794,
  "ContentType": "application/octet-stream",
  "ETag": "\"...\""
}
```

ci-bot: Onboard job #142 failed: checksum mismatch on part 3 — see CI logs: https://ci.local/builds/142 (auth required).

raj: That ContentLength is the tell. If HF -> CF -> S3 chain applied gzip/encoding or range requests got messed up, the object on S3 could be the truncated artifact. Try re-downloading with `curl -L --compress` from the origin URL and compare sizes locally before uploading. Also confirm the registry presign flagged `s3_presign=true` for mirror uploads.

ana: I tried re-download with `curl -L --compressed` and the file size locally is 524288000 (matches HF). However the CI upload step used `aws s3 cp` from the container; I see `--content-encoding` wasn't set. Re-uploading now with `--content-encoding identity` to avoid CF gzip.

mike: For the tokenizer issue, quick fix: `jq '.bos_token = "<s>" | .eos_token = "</s>"' tokenizer.json > tokenizer.fixed.json` then run `python3 tools/validate_tokenizer.py tokenizer.fixed.json`. We'll add that as a compatibility transform in the loader.

tess: I'll add two lints to the onboarding pipeline: 1) assert tokenizer.bos_token and eos_token are non-null, 2) assert S3 head-object ContentLength == manifest.size after upload. Also pin presign TTL >=3600 for HF-origin mirrors to reduce race-y presign redirects.

oliver: Who needs mirror-write in the registry to re-run the ingest? We shouldn't keep re-uploading from dev machines. Create IAM role `mirror-uploader` and grant the registry service principal write. @infra-bot please.

infra-bot: Ticket #789 created: request IAM role `mirror-uploader` for eng-ml with S3 PutObject+KMS:Encrypt permissions on `redwood-artifacts/staging/*`. ETA 2 business days.

ana: Re-upload succeeded using `--content-encoding identity` and new presign TTL. Head-object now shows 524288000 and sha256 matches HF. Re-triggered onboard job; CI passed tokenizer check after I applied jq fix.

mike: Nice. Can we also add a small unit test that simulates CF adding gzip header and ensures upload sets identity if content already compressed?

tess: Yep — adding tests and updating the onboarding docs in `docs/onboarding.md` with presign guidance. I'll create a follow-up PR.

oliver: I'll track the IAM ticket and assign mirror ownership to eng-ml once infra signs off. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

ana: Thanks everyone :thumbsup: I'll close the registry ticket once mirror-uploader role exists and the CI onboard is green.

raj: :eyes: great follow-up.

ci-bot: Job #142 re-run passed. Artifact tagged `onboarded:2026-03-18`.

infra-bot: Updating ticket #789 — pre-approvals recorded, awaiting final manual review.

ana: Closing loop: will post a short checklist in #eng-ml with steps to avoid this in future.
